blocks.text: Intensity is defined as the amount of energy transmitted per unit area per unit time in the direction of propagation of progressive wave. It is a measure of the power of a wave and is usually denoted by the symbol "I". It is measured in units of watts per square meter (W m⁻²).

A progressive wave or travelling wave is one that travels through a medium in a consistent direction and transferring energy from one point to another. It is a wave that propagates or moves forward, as opposed to a stationary or standing wave. Examples of progressive waves include water waves, sound waves, light waves etc.
By definition, the intensity of a wave, is

items: I = Intensity of wave in (W m⁻²)

blocks.title: Example 7.8
blocks.problem:
(a) A wave has an intensity of 0.5 W m⁻² at a distance of 3.0 m from the source. What is the power of the wave?
(b) Two progressive waves have intensities of 0.5 W m⁻² and 0.25 W m⁻². Find total intensities of two waves.
steps:
(b)   I₁ = 0.5 W m⁻²
I₂ = 0.25 W m⁻²
I = ?
I = I₁ + I₂
I = 0.5 + 0.25

blocks.title: Tidbits
blocks.text: Frequency and amplitude of a travelling wave are independent of each other. That is why you can turn up the volume of a song (increase amplitude) without changing its pitch (which depends on frequency).

blocks.title: Brain Teaser
blocks.text: Can you find the decibel level of a travelling wave whose intensity is 10 W m⁻²?

blocks.title: Example 7.9
blocks.problem: A speaker is emitting sound waves with a power of 50 watts. If the sound waves are spreading out evenly in all directions and the intensity of the sound waves is measured at a distance of 5 m from the speaker, what is the intensity of the sound waves if the area of the sphere (the surface area of a sphere) at that distance is approximately 314 m²?
steps:
Intensity = Power/Area
I = P/A
I = 50 W/314 m²

blocks.title: Tidbits
blocks.text: Sound cannot travel through vacuum, as there are no particles to transmit the sound wave.
